《命运石之门》（Steins;Gate）最初由5pb.和Nitroplus于2009年在Xbox 360平台发售，后陆续移植到PC、PSP、PS3、PSV、PS4、Switch乃至手机平台。作为科学ADV系列的第二部作品（前作为《混沌之脑》），这部以“假想科学ADV”为旗号的视觉小说，不仅是MAGES.社最具代表性的作品之一，也被许多玩家奉为“时间旅行题材的巅峰之作”。

故事：混沌之上的牵绊
故事发生在东京秋叶原——御宅族文化的圣地。自称“疯狂科学家”的中二病大学生冈部伦太郎，与伙伴们组成了“未来道具研究所”。一次偶然的实验中，他们发现了通过手机微波炉和电脑配合，可以向过去发送邮件从而改变历史的能力——D-Mail。

然而，看似简单的改变背后，蝴蝶效应悄然展开。当冈部和他的伙伴们在喜悦与好奇中一次次尝试修改过去时，他们逐渐发现：每一次干预都像抽去积木塔中的木块，整个世界正缓慢地走向崩塌——最核心的那根积木，是青梅竹马椎名真由理的“死亡命运”。

游戏分为明确的两个阶段：前六章的“日常篇”与第七章开始的“悬疑篇”。许多初玩者会对前半部分略显冗长的日常铺垫感到耐心不足——这正是本作最具争议也最精妙的设计。当命运的齿轮开始逆转，玩家会无比怀念那些看似无聊的实验室嬉闹时光。这种“失去后才懂得珍惜”的情感冲击，正是剧本设计的高明之处。

玩法：走向唯一真实的“世界线”
作为视觉小说，《命运石之门》的核心玩法在于“手机触发系统”——玩家通过决定是否接听电话、回复哪条短信、发送或不发送D-Mail，来影响世界线的走向。

需要特别指出的是，这并非传统意义上“自由度高”的多结局游戏。游戏设有六个结局，但通往真结局（“境界面上的命运石之门”）有着严格的触发顺序。绝大多数玩家若不依赖攻略，几乎不可能在一次通关中进入真结局——这在设计上存在一定争议，有人认为是深度设计，也有人批评其为“刻意为难玩家”。

但换个角度看，这种设计恰如其分地契合了主题：在无数次失败与轮回中摸索唯一正确的路径，本身就是对“命运”一词最深刻的体验。

角色：每一个齿轮都有自己的重量
冈部伦太郎 —— 表面上是扮演“凤凰院凶真”的狂妄中二病，骨子里却是甘愿承受万般痛苦来守护伙伴的温柔少年。宫野真守的配音堪称教科书级别，从癫狂的笑声到绝望的嘶吼，情绪跨度之大令人叹服。

牧濑红莉栖 —— “助手”克里斯蒂娜，傲娇系角色的标杆。她与冈部之间的斗智与互动，是游戏情感线的核心支柱。当那句“你是我的助手，永远都是”响起时，无论多少次重温，都无法不动容。

椎名真由理 —— “嘟嘟噜”。表面上只是天真无邪的吉祥物，但她的存在是整部作品最大的情感锚点。当她一次次以各种方式死去，冈部的每一次崩溃，都直击玩家内心。

桥田至 —— “桶子”。御宅族黑客，承担了几乎所有技术实现与笑点调剂，但在关键时刻展现出惊人的靠谱。

桐生萌郁 —— “闪光指压师”。沉默寡言的手机重度用户，她背后的秘密是故事中期最大的反转之一。

漆原琉华 —— 伪娘巫女，关于性别的D-Mail引发了一场关于“何为真实自我”的哲学讨论。

菲利斯·喵喵 —— 秋叶原女王，她的故事触及了“用个人记忆换取世界改变”的残酷命题。

每位角色都不是简单的标签堆砌。随着世界线的变动，他们展现出不同面貌，而这些变化恰恰构成了游戏对“人究竟由什么定义”的追问。

主题：科学与神话的交汇
《命运石之门》最可贵之处，在于它试图用现代人能理解的“科学语言”去重构古老的神话母题：

世界线：不同于传统“平行世界”理论，本作采用了“单一世界线重构”模型——过去改变时，整个世界被“覆盖”而非“分裂”。这既规避了平行宇宙的虚无主义陷阱，也为冈部的痛苦赋予了重量：每一次改变都是对自己记忆的背叛。

世界线收束：某些重大事件（如真由理之死）是被“命运”锁死的——无论怎么改变细节，结果终究会以另一种形式降临。这一设定既符合“神话中的宿命论”，又为“打破收束”提供了终极悬念。

Reading Steiner：冈部独有的能力——能在世界线变动后保留其他线的记忆。这既是祝福也是诅咒：他是唯一记得那些“消失了的未来”的人。

最精彩的设定在于：故事中的“科学理论”（如Kerr黑洞、裸奇点、LHC实验）并非凭空杜撰，而是在真实物理学理论基础上进行的“合理幻想”。游戏甚至会引用约翰·提托（John Titor）的真实网络传奇作为叙事线索，让玩家产生“这一切或许真的可能发生”的错觉。

画面：立绘画风由huke负责，其厚涂风格与略显暗沉的色调，营造出独特的忧郁与神秘氛围。但早期版本的立绘动态效果极少，角色表情切换略显生硬。后续推出的“Elite”版（2018年）改用动画版画面，流畅度大幅提升，但也有人觉得丧失了原画的独特质感。

音乐：阿保刚的配乐是无可争议的杰作。从充满希望的《Gate of Steiner》到窒息般压抑的《Believe Me》，再到每次真由理死亡时响起的《Silent Sorrow》，音乐与叙事的结合达到了“听前奏即泪目”的程度。片头曲《Hacking to the Gate》给人留下了尤为深刻的印象。

争议与批评
慢热问题：这一点无法回避。前五章的大量日常内容对一些玩家来说可能构成劝退门槛。但需要区分“无意义的拖沓”与“有目的的铺垫”——本作更接近后者。

剧情锁设计：强行要求玩家先完成五个非真结局才能解锁真结局，在叙事体验上反而破坏了情感连贯性。Elite版对此有所调整。

结语：
评价《命运石之门》是困难的。若仅以“游戏性”衡量，它几乎不及格——缺乏传统意义的挑战、操作极度简化、选择系统古板。但若作为“互动叙事作品”来看待，它无疑是殿堂级的。

当最终ED响起，当冈部跨越无数世界线、背负所有记忆的重量、终于抓住那一线可能——你得到的不仅是一次“通关”的满足，而是对“选择与代价”“记忆与存在”“命运与自由”这些命题沉甸甸的感悟。

许多年后，你可能忘记了D-Mail的具体机制，忘记了世界线变动的数值，但你不会忘记：在那个实验室里，一群年轻人用最笨拙也最勇敢的方式，对抗着名为“命运”的洪流。

Steins;Gate is my favourite anime of all time. I first watched it in 2018, in anticipation of Steins;Gate 0 and fell in love with the series. It's one of, if not, the best time travel stories I've ever experienced.

I've never gotten around to reading Visual Novels in general and only started this year, so I only managed to get myself to read the Steins;Gate VN now despite having rewatched the anime multiple times already. And all I can say is, this Visual Novel is absolutely freaking fantastic.

I can see the changes the anime made to take advantage of the anime medium, and I can see what the VN has done to take advantage of its own medium. Both the anime and the VN are absolutely different experiences of a more or less, same story. If you have watched the anime, I absolutely recommend playing the VN as well for the experience. If you haven't watched the anime yet, well, what are you waiting for? This will be an absolutely amazing experience as long as you don't stop before Chapter 5.

The Chapter 5 (Episode 1-11) dilemma is that a lot of people say this first half is very slow. I have personally never understood this because I was hooked since the first episode / chapter. It feels slow because the first half is very character driven, where the story tries to get you to know the characters. Because once the second half hits, it hits HARD. Especially once you've started liking characters from the build up. Furthermore, the first half also builds up a lot of the suspense and technology/science used for the time machine which becomes more and more relevant in the second half.

Rather than worrying about the first half being slow, I feel like it's difficult to get into Steins;Gate due to Otaku culture / terminologies that non-anime fans may not already be familiar with. This may be what turns people off / away from the series, rather than the first half being slow. For me, because I was already an anime fan, I understood just about all the terms and references without any issue which did enhance my enjoyment of the series.

In summary, Steins;Gate is a masterpiece of a time travel story. And everyone who hasn't experienced it absolutely should, but you should have a bit of patience and the ability to accept cultural / terminological differences.

One of the best visual novels out there,
A unique spin on popular conspiracy theories,
A time capsule to early internet culture, 
And translations that sort of bum me out. 

It’s been said time and time again so I won’t say much on it, but this really is one of the best written visual novels of all time.
The characters definitely aren’t going to be for everyone, and admittedly can be grating at times, but I still appreciate the way they’re written. 
I watched the anime before I went through the VN and it was still well worth it, and now this is my second play through after several years and it still holds up. 

What I appreciate most about this VN is that it is ironically a really unique look into the past, specifically internet and otaku culture of the late 2000’s. You get a bit of that from the anime, but it goes DEEP into it in the game. 
Back when I first interacted with Steins Gate in 2013 or 14 the internet slang in use was already outdated and I couldn’t catch every reference, now it’s downright archaic and so I’m really grateful for the in game encyclopedia. Some might say the heavy focus on the internet culture of the era makes this VN feel extremely dated, and I can understand that sentiment, but for me it really is like a Time Machine. This VN inadvertently(?) does such a good job of preserving a period of time for this particular subculture in such a way that it really does feel like stepping back into a time period that primarily exists in the memories of people who were on the internet at that time. 
I can’t imagine it has as much charm if you weren’t a netizen around 2009 though.
While it might be unique to see, the nostalgia factor probably plays a heavy hand here. 

This VN also weaves in real life conspiracy theories around real life entities like SERN so well that at times it makes me feel paranoid, and it introduces you to some fun deep dives like John Titor if you weren’t already familiar with that sort of thing. 

My only major complaint about this VN is the translations. I don’t understand enough of the language to play VN’s in Japanese yet, but I do understand enough to be able to tell that some of the translations are off. 
I get that literal translations are usually not the way to go, and localization is and always has been a tricky thing, and at the time it was probably even more difficult, but still it can be a bit of a letdown to read the text, hear the voice actors and just think “yeah that is not what they just said”

Aside from that very minor complaint this is hands down one of my favorite VN’s of all time, and I highly recommend Steins Gate to anyone who is even remotely interested or curious about it, even if you already know the story. 
It is well worth the time investment.

For me, Steins;Gate is my all time favorite. I watched the anime first, and I still think starting with the anime is the better experience. At the same time, though, I have to say that the visual novel introduces many story elements differently, and whether those changes are better or worse depends on the person. Personally, I enjoyed both versions.
I think the anime was a surprisingly good adaptation of the visual novel, but ultimately, it’s objectively better to experience the original story in its fullest form. The anime removed too many conversations and couldn’t include the different endings that the visual novel had, so keep that in mind.
